    • Sentence B will be the next sentence because it is connected with the previous sentence and further tells us about when and where the turtles laid their eggs.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in Direct Speech. As per the question we have to change it into Indirect Speech. 
  • The process of transformation is as follows:
    • The given sentence is an example of an imperative sentence.
    • Let's look at the rules of transformation:
      • While changing the narration of an imperative sentence, we need to follow the given steps:
      • The conjunction 'to' should be used in place of a comma (,) and inverted commas (“ ”). 
      • Here, 'don't' will be changed into 'not to'.
      • 'said to' will be changed into 'told'.
      • 'to' is followed by 'V1 (wear)'.
      • Lastly, the adverb 'here' will be changed into 'there'. 
    • Example: 
      • The queen said to his servant, "Cook me some delicious food today." (Direct Speech)
      • The queen ordered his servant to cook her some delicious food that day. (Indirect Speech)
         

Correct Sentence: She told them not to smoke there.

Hinglish

  • परिवर्तन की प्रक्रिया इस प्रकार है:
    • दिया गया वाक्य Imperative Sentence का उदाहरण है।
    • आइए परिवर्तन के नियमों को देखें:
      • एक Imperative Sentence का Narration बदलते समय, हमें दिए गए चरणों का पालन करना होगा:
      • दिए गए वाक्य की धारणा 'request' है।
      • संयोजन 'to' का प्रयोग अल्पविराम (,) और उल्टे अल्पविराम (" ") के स्थान पर किया जाना चाहिए।
      • यहां, 'don't' को 'not to' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
      • 'said to' को 'told' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
      • 'to' के बाद 'V1' आता है।
      • अंत में, Adverb 'here' को 'there' में बदल दिया जाएगा।
    • Example:
      • The queen said to his servant, "Cook me some delicious food today." (Direct Speech)
      • The queen ordered his servant to cook her some delicious food that day. (Indirect Speech)

questions.question: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order. A. More than 134,000 people have been evacuated to safe areas. B. questions.questionHtml:

A. More than 134,000 people have been evacuated to safe areas.

Key Points

  • We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
    • Sentence D will be the first sentence because it is an introductory sentence telling us about 'Mount Agung'.
    • After it, Sentence C will be used because it further tells us about the expected eruption of the volcano in two days.
    • Sentence A will be the next sentence because it is connected with the previous sentence as it tells us that more than '1,34,000' people have been evacuated to safe areas. (as the volcano is expected to erupt in 2 days)
    • Lastly, Sentence B will be used.
    • Thus, the correct sequence is:
      • D: Mount Agung is a volcano on the popular tourist island of Bali in Indonesia.
      • C: The volcano is expected to erupt within two days.
      • A: More than 134,000 people have been evacuated to safe areas.
      • B: They are now far away from the volcano.
         

Correct Sequence: Mount Agung is a volcano on the popular tourist island of Bali in Indonesia. The volcano is expected to erupt within two days. More than 134,000 people have been evacuated to safe areas. They are now far away from the volcano.

Additional Information

  • Gerunds are formed by adding '-ing' to the verb: 'sleeping, 'drawing,' 'swimming.' But they are not the '-ing' verb forms that you see in the present or past continuous tense. They look the same, but gerunds are actually verb forms used as nouns.
  • Let’s take the infinitive of the verb “to sleep” and use it in two different sentences:
    • I am sleeping.
  • This is the present continuous. “Sleeping” here is part of the verb. It is not a gerund. Here’s the second sentence:
    • I don’t like sleeping.
  • This is present simple, but it contains a gerund. “Sleeping” is the direct object of this sentence.

Hinglish

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to improve it, select ‘No improvement required’. The report, that markets are open, is not true.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to improve it, select ‘No improvement required’.

The report, that markets are open, is not true.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is No improvement is required.

Key Points

  • As the subject of the clause is markets which is a plural, the verb should be in plural form(are).
  • Hence, the sentence is correct.
  • The correct answer is option 3.
  • We can think that markets are open is wrong because of the rule of "are should be followed by past participle"
  • But here the word open is not in passive voice.
  • Here There is a news (report) which is saying that markets are open.

Confusion Points

  • Such as Class is open
  • Class is closed
  • In the same way here the report which said that the markets are open is not true.
  • The report is antecedent and that markets are open is a dependent clause.
  • So The use of is according to the Subject the Report is correct.

Additional Information

  •  Relative Pronouns
    • ​A relative pronoun is a word that introduces a dependent (or relative) clause and connects it to an independent clause. A clause beginning with a relative pronoun is poised to answer questions such as Which one? How many? or What kind? Who, whom, what, which, and that are all relative pronouns.
    • Who: Refers to a person (as the verb’s subject)
    • Whom: Refers to a person (as the verb’s object)
    • Which: Refers to an animal or thing
    • What: Refers to a nonliving thing
    • That: Refers to a person, animal, or thing

    • The woman who came to the door left flowers for you.
